title: The Five Gestures of the Covenant: How the Rational Is Sent Out and Brought Home
reading:
A question is put: the small customs by which people greet one another in the world — the wish of peace, the offering of the right hand, the embrace, the bow, the laying on of hands by which a humble man is honored and made a lord — to whom do these belong? Why do we do them?

The answer: these five gestures, which look like trifling things in daily life, are in truth great. They are the five mysteries of the Divine Human, the five marks of the covenant by which the rational is sent out from the Lord into its contest with the proprium and brought home again. What the soul performs visibly toward its neighbor is the outer trace of what the Lord performs inwardly toward the soul itself.

The first peace is the peace given to the rational as it sets out — the settled accord of the divine angels of the inmost state walking with it, running to meet it, putting their peace and their hand and their blessing and their joy upon it before it goes down into the contest. The first right hand is the strengthening that the life-bearing principle of the Lord places into the rational at the moment of its going forth, the operative power by which it can stand. The first embrace is the union of love by which that same life-bearing principle holds the rational close at the moment of separation, and by which all the orders of the inmost state, and the household of the rational's own kindred, send it out wrapped in love and affection. The first obeisance is the rational's own bowing — bending its knee toward the God of Truth and the whole inmost state to ask, before it descends, for the power by which it will be saved and brought back. The first laying on of hands is the act by which the life-bearing principle arms the rational, girds it strongly, sets its hand upon its head, and commissions it to the contest. So armed, it goes down, and finishes its struggle with the proprium and its enmity.

In these five signs, in these five mysteries, the rational came forth from the inmost state against the proprium, humbled it, and prevailed.

And at the time when it came up again out of the war and entered into the kingdom of its own household, it came up in these same five mysteries. The peace it returned in is the same peace the call had given it when it was first sent out from the Lord of life — the peace it carried down into the natural under the proprium's rule is the very peace it carried back. So too the right hand: the Lord's operative power that armed it for descent is the operative power that brought it up out of the battle. So too the embrace: as the life-bearing principle had embraced it at the going out, so the Father and Mother of life embraced it at the coming up. So too the bow: the rational that had bowed before going down bowed again before the God of Truth, in the gaze of the blessed states, when the Father and Mother of life had brought it up out of the deep. And the laying on of hands at the return: when the Lord's operative power had carried the rational up out of all the waves and given it rest among the great inmost states of its kindred, it set the rational on its feet before the Father, and a voice came down from on high: Sit, my son, my firstborn, at my right hand until I make all your enemies a footstool under your feet. So it received the great laying-on by which it became the leader of its brothers in the new aeon.

These five mysteries, which were first established in the divine and were the first to be received in the midst of the proprium's powers, are the same five by which every soul is brought home. At the time of its going forth, the form of light comes out before it and draws it out of the darkness toward the light. The form of light stills the soul with the kiss and with her stillness, away from the disordered loves that surround the body. In her likeness, in her image, the inner self that is coming forth from the body is brought to peace. After this, the bearer of the prize stretches forth his right hand and draws the soul up out of the depth of the body, and receives it home with the kiss and the embrace. That soul worships its redeemer, who is the form of light, and in that very moment is completed with what belongs to it — entering the house of the Living Ones, among the angels, to receive the crown of glory in life forever.

So the small gestures of peace and greeting, of hand and embrace and bow and blessing, are not trifles. They are the visible echo, given to us in the world, of the whole covenant by which the soul is sent out, sustained through its contest, and received back into the inmost.
